# google_bigtable_memory_layer

Enables and manages the memory layer for a Cloud Bigtable cluster.

Creation of this resource enables the memory layer on the specified cluster (`ENTERPRISE_PLUS` and `SSD` storage type required). Destruction of this resource disables the memory layer on the cluster.


To get more information about MemoryLayer, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/reference/admin/rest/v2/MemoryLayer)

## Example Usage - Bigtable Memory Layer


```hcl
resource "google_bigtable_instance" "instance" {
  name          = "bt-instance"
  instance_type = "PRODUCTION"
  edition       = "ENTERPRISE_PLUS"
  cluster {
    cluster_id   = "bt-cluster"
    zone         = "us-central1-b"
    num_nodes    = 1
    storage_type = "SSD"
  }

  deletion_protection = false
}

resource "google_bigtable_memory_layer" "memory_layer" {
  instance = google_bigtable_instance.instance.name
  cluster  = google_bigtable_instance.instance.cluster[0].cluster_id
}

resource "google_bigtable_app_profile" "ap" {
  instance       = google_bigtable_instance.instance.name
  app_profile_id = "bt-profile"

  single_cluster_routing {
    cluster_id                 = google_bigtable_memory_layer.memory_layer.cluster
    allow_transactional_writes = true
  }

  standard_isolation {
    priority = "PRIORITY_LOW"
    memory_config {}
  }

  ignore_warnings = true
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `instance` -
  (Required)
  The name of the instance to enable the memory layer within.

* `cluster` -
  (Required)
  The ID of the cluster to enable the memory layer on.


* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/instances/{{instance}}/clusters/{{cluster}}/memoryLayer`

* `name` -
  The unique name of the memory layer. Values are of the form `projects/<project>/instances/<instance>/clusters/<cluster>/memoryLayer`.

* `etag` -
  System-generated token used by the server to ensure that the client has an up-to-date value before proceeding.

* `state` -
  The current state of the memory layer.

* `memory_config` -
  The memory configuration for the cluster.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_memory_config).


<a name="nested_memory_config"></a>The `memory_config` block contains:

* `storage_size_gib` -
  (Output)
  Reporting the current size of the memory layer in GiB.

## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 60 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 60 minutes.

## Import


MemoryLayer can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/instances/{{instance}}/clusters/{{cluster}}/memoryLayer`
* `{{project}}/{{instance}}/{{cluster}}`
* `{{instance}}/{{cluster}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import MemoryLayer using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    instance = "<-required value->"
    cluster = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_bigtable_memory_layer.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import MemoryLayer using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/instances/{{instance}}/clusters/{{cluster}}/memoryLayer"
  to = google_bigtable_memory_layer.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), MemoryLayer can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_bigtable_memory_layer.default projects/{{project}}/instances/{{instance}}/clusters/{{cluster}}/memoryLayer
$ terraform import google_bigtable_memory_layer.default {{project}}/{{instance}}/{{cluster}}
$ terraform import google_bigtable_memory_layer.default {{instance}}/{{cluster}}
```
